title: The Case of the Wobbly Glass Animals
markdown:
The sun peeked over the horizon, a butterscotch disc painting the sky in apricot and rose. Rafi, a sand fox with fur the colour of dawn, stretched. His whiskers twitched. Something felt different. Not the usual market carts rumbling, or the sleepy coo of doves. This was a quiet deep hum. A secret whisper.

Rafi padded to the windowsill, his paws silent. He gasped.

The tiny glass animals. The giraffe, its long neck usually straight. The pig, always round and cheerful. The speedy rabbit, poised to dash. They were sagging. Like butter in the sun. The giraffe’s neck bowed. The pig looked as if it had rolled downhill. Their shapes lost their crisp definition. Peculiar. Very peculiar. Rafi had seen many mornings, but never one like this.

"Tika." Rafi yipped, a sharp excited note. "Tika, you must see this. It is baffling."

Emerald and sapphire feathers burst from the market stall next door. Tika the parrot, a dazzling splash of colour, preened a brilliant blue feather. "See what, Rafi? Another dusty beetle? Honestly. Buzz off, I say."

"No, no, Tika. Not beetles." Rafi’s tail flicked. "The glass. Look. They are all peculiar."

Tika hopped closer, beady eyes widening. "By my tail feathers. They are wobbly-wobbly." His voice a pitch higher. He tilted his head, as if listening. "And they are warm. Just a whisper of heat."

Rafi nudged a tiny glass sparrow. It felt yielding, almost soft. "They are melting, Tika. Slowly. But why? What makes them melt?"

Tika flapped his wings, a tiny whirlwind of colour. "Melting glass needs heat, Rafi. Lots of it. More than this morning sun. This is a different kind of warmth. A purposeful warmth." He hopped onto Rafi’s back. Rafi barely felt his weight. "Let us investigate, my sandy friend. We will be the great Glass Detectives."

They scrambled down. Rafi’s paws were soft on the dusty ground. Tika, a vibrant jewel on his back, kept a sharp lookout. They crept toward the market square. The air grew warmer. A faint metallic scent, like hot iron with something sweet and strange, drifted on the breeze. Beneath the market carts’ clatter, a rhythmic thump-thump-thump echoed. A deep beat. Like a giant sleepy heart.

"What is that beat, Tika?" Rafi whispered. His ears swiveled.

"Sounds like a giant heart. Or perhaps a furnace. A very big, active furnace."

They tiptoed toward an old alleyway behind the spice stalls. Cinnamon and star anise usually filled the air. Today a different aroma dominated, stronger. The heat intensified. The pulsing grew louder, vibrating through Rafi’s paws. Rafi sniffed. Intense warmth, like a baker’s oven working overtime, but much hotter.

"Down there." Tika pointed with a sharp claw. A loose stone near an overflowing bin. A faint pulsating orange light glowed from the crack. A secret eye.

Rafi nudged the stone with his snout. Tika pecked at its edges. Creak. The stone shifted. A dark opening appeared. A wave of potent heat billowed up, carrying the scent of molten glass, rich and sharp.

"Wow." Rafi breathed. The heat was intense, yet inviting.

"Spectacular." Tika’s feathers ruffled.

They peered down. Below was a cavernous space, glowing with deep vibrant orange light, pulsing like liquid fire. In the centre, a massive furnace roared, spitting flames. Around the edges, glinting in the light, were tools. Delicate carved metal tools. One, apart from the others, caught Rafi’s eye. A tiny delicate fork, its prongs impossibly fine.

"Look. It looks as if it is for shaping something very carefully. Like a comb for a tiny head."

Tika hopped onto the edge. He tilted his head, scanning the stone. He pecked at a faded inscription. "It says Murano. Murano. The finest glass. Uncle Pip told stories of Murano glass."

Rafi’s tail gave a vigorous wag. "Murano glass. So that is it. These animals were crafted by master glassmakers. Using these amazing tools." He imagined nimble fingers working with fire and sand.

The heat was intense, swirling, but not frightening. It felt like the heart of creation. The glass animals had softened because of this warmth, this ancient powerful art form hidden beneath their feet.

"This is incredible." Tika’s feathers puffed out with wonder. "A secret furnace. Murano glass. Imagine the stories these tools could tell."

Rafi felt a thrill course through him. Pure discovery. The mystery of the sagging animals had led them to something extraordinary. "We should learn more, Tika. About Murano. I want to know how they make things so delicate."

"Indeed we should, my clever fox. Our detective work has only just begun. Who knows what other secrets lie hidden."

And with a shared look of pure curiosity, Rafi the sand fox and Tika the market parrot turned, tails wagging, wings fluttering, ready to discover more wonders. The furnace kept its orange pulse, and the little animals on the sill, having been a little too near the secret, slowly remembered their shapes.
